sam: Quick heads-up — after merging the kernel-adapter change in main I'm seeing an 18-25% p99 token latency regression on long chat sessions with paged KV. Reproducer below, running on a small flash pool. :frowning:

sam: repro (local w/ small model):
```
export REDWOOD_ENV=local
./bench_tool --model paged-flash-8B --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kv-mode paged --kernel-adapter on --duration 300
```

sam: logs show repeated eviction spikes and a lot of small IO write bursts around the block-table handoff.

jia: ugh. can you paste the relevant slab/evict logs? also which kernel variant did you pick? flashv2?

sam: flashv2-compat adapter. snippet from runtime log:
```
[2026-03-10T12:04:22Z] kv_pager: eviction: victim slab=3 blocks=128 reason=alloc_wait
[2026-03-10T12:04:22Z] kernel_adapter: switched kernel=flashv2_compat -> flashv1_fallback latency=3.2ms
[2026-03-10T12:04:22Z] io_coalesce: flush small_writes=62 total_bytes=124KB
```

alex: can you run with perf sampling + kv residency telemetry? I want to see hotpaths. run `./perf_sampler --pid $PID --out flame.svg --symbols` and grab kv-telemetry from /tmp/kvstats.json

sam: attached kv stats (excerpt):
```
allocated_blocks: 10240
pinned_blocks: 2048
page_faults_1min: 412
avg_alloc_latency_ms: 0.87
evict_cycles_1min: 97
```

maria: looks like the alloc strategy is falling back to slab-slow path frequently. try bumping `pager.alloc_watermark` to 0.6 and `kernel.batch_threshold_ms` down to 1.5.

maria: config example:
```
pager:
  mode: paged
  alloc_watermark: 0.6
  eviction_policy: lru_chunked
kernel_adapter:
  batch_threshold_ms: 1.5
  prefer_flashv2: true
```

sam: tried that, p99 improved ~6% but still ~12% above baseline. flame shows a lot of time in `blocktable::rechain` and `kv_pager::page_in`.

alex: can you post a tiny perf sample (top stacks)?

sam: top stacks (counts):
```
2000 kv_pager::page_in
1500 blocktable::rechain
800 kernel_adapter::select_kernel
400 io_coalesce::flush
```

perf-bot: telemetry summary (last 5m) for run 4205000000: p50=52ms p95=120ms p99=392ms tail_ops=1.7% io_write_bursts=63

jia: hypothesis: when kernel adapter flips between flashv2 and fallback we lose batching opportunities and trigger more frequent small allocs. That + our current eviction hysteresis leads to thrash.

maria: agree. idea: make kernel switch idempotent per request group and introduce a short sticky window (e.g., 200ms) before switching back. also increase `alloc_reserve` for hot slotmap shards.

sam: would be good to test two patches: (A) sticky kernel window, (B) raise alloc_reserve to keep pinned blocks. can we A/B in staging?

ops-bot: created staging roll `staging/paged-kernel-stick` -> deploy queued. :rocket:

alex: I'll add a lightweight microbenchmark that simulates long-seq chats + mixed cold-hot KV access to the bench suite.

sam: thanks. I'll capture a full flame and kv dump once staging is up. tagging @maria @jia for follow-up. :eyes:

maria: acked, will prepare patch for sticky window and alloc tuning. planning to run 4 stress runs overnight.

jia: if we end up needing a structural change to blocktable rechain we should open a design RFC, but try config + sticky adapter first.

sam: cool. marking this thread for follow-ups. thanks everyone.
